tasks.short: Design and implement supply chain changes that meet environmental policies.

steps.what: Read environmental policies and identify supply chain requirements.

loop.input: Approved environmental policy and customer requirements.
loop.output: Draft environmental design brief with source passages and unresolved requirements.
loop.check: Manager verifies scope, obligations and source citations before accepting the brief.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved requirements go to the policy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in prose and need interpretation across documents.

steps.what: Export purchasing, inventory value and transport costs from the {ERP}.
Export shipment, stock movement and production activity from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate baseline impacts and compare network, sourcing and inventory scenarios.
Discuss environmental gains, service risks, cost and operational feasibility.
Write the implementation plan, responsibilities, measures and proposed operating changes.

loop.input: Preferred scenario, recorded conditions and approved plan template.
loop.output: Draft change plan with linked decisions, owners and unresolved items.
loop.check: Validate figures against the scenario dataset; manager checks responsibilities and feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing commitments remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: The plan must turn discussion notes and conditions into readable implementation instructions.

steps.what: Approve the investment, service tradeoffs and implementation scope.
Coordinate operating changes and check implementation milestones in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a versioned scenario calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, displayed through the {BI}. Bounded loops draft the policy brief and change plan with source references; managers choose tradeoffs and approve commitments. The {PROJECT} tracks approved changes, dependencies and exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activity data, cost records and environmental factors used different units and boundaries. Teams rebuilt comparisons for each project.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting interfaces and faster development make reusable mappings, calculations and approval records cheaper to build. Bounded document extraction reduces preparation work.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier environmental evidence may be incomplete. Environmental factors, service resilience and investment choices still need defensible assumptions and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose acceptable tradeoffs and secure commitments from teams that bear the operational consequences.

ambition.what: Quarterly review of transport consolidation options against cost, service and environmental targets.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling comparisons and more time testing choices with operations. They can propose quarterly adjustments within an explicitly delegated operating budget; investment approval stays with the operations director.

reach.learn: Shipment grouping, route constraints, factor boundaries and sensitivity analysis.
Milestone acceptance, dependency management and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: A sponsored routing case reports fewer kilometres per pallet; it does not establish environmental compliance.
Versioned calculations can compare cost, service and estimated environmental effects without an autonomous agent.

assumptions: The company operates a physical supply chain and has approved environmental policies.
Time shares describe active task effort across contributing roles, excluding waiting between project stages.
Environmental factors have an agreed owner, scope and version.
Operational changes receive any consultation required by national rules before implementation.
Access design follows GDPR where records contain personal data; EU AI Act applicability is assessed for the actual use.
unknowns: Available exports, interfaces and integration permissions.
Environmental targets, calculation boundaries and acceptable evidence.
Who can approve investment and operating changes.
Whether workplace changes require employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which environmental factors match the actual transport modes, materials and reporting boundary?
Can scenario recommendations be reconciled against historical operating results?
new_work: Maintain activity mappings and environmental factor versions.
Review extracted requirements and drafted implementation plans.
Investigate missing data and implausible scenario results.
Track whether implemented changes achieve the expected effects.

tasks.short: Forecast material costs and maintain approved standard cost lists.

steps.what: Export purchase prices, material usage and existing standards from the {ERP}.
Read supplier quotations and price notices received through the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Supplier quotations and price notices, including attachments.
loop.output: Draft rates with currency, unit, validity, quantity breaks and source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and arithmetic; review changed rates and ambiguous commercial terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguous or incomplete rates remain excluded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Suppliers use inconsistent documents and describe price conditions in free text.

steps.what: Normalise currencies, units, freight and duties in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree forecast assumptions for volume, yield, exchange rates and supplier changes.
Calculate material forecasts, proposed standards and changes from current costs.
Review cost changes and approve the standard cost list.
Load approved standard costs and effective dates into the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configured extracts from the {ERP} feed a versioned cost calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}; a bounded loop turns quotations from the {EMAIL} into reviewable rate records. Deterministic calculations produce forecasts, sensitivities and proposed standards, with assumptions visible in the {BI}. The {WORKFLOW} records finance approval and releases only that approved version to the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier formats varied, unit conversions lived in individual workbooks, and approval records were separate from uploaded costs.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster development lowers the cost of reusable conversion rules, source-linked quotation extraction and controlled publication. Standard costing functionality already exists in many {ERP} deployments.
tasks.still_hard: Future prices, yield losses and purchasing volumes remain uncertain. Finance must decide which assumptions are appropriate for official standards.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a temporary price movement from a lasting cost change and challenge commercially weak assumptions.

ambition.what: Monthly material cost sensitivity review for purchasing and margin decisions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding cost lists and more time testing price and yield exposure. They can recommend purchasing responses within existing authority; finance retains approval of official standards.

reach.task: Estimate material exposure under alternative production schedules.
reach.learn: Bills of materials, yield assumptions and the timing of material consumption.
Separate price, volume, mix and exchange-rate effects.

evidence.claim: Cost normalisation, scenario arithmetic and approved-version publication can use deterministic calculations and existing controls.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare quotation fields, but ambiguous terms still require review.

assumptions: The company maintains material identifiers, purchasing history and an established costing policy.
Time shares describe active task effort across contributing roles.
Approved standards can be imported with effective dates and an audit trail.
Access uses least privilege and GDPR safeguards for supplier contact data.
The access range includes checking consultation duties under national rules; workforce assessment is outside scope.
unknowns: Whether standard costs use purchase price, landed cost or another approved basis.
Available {ERP} costing configuration and import controls.
Quality of unit conversions, material identifiers and quotation history.
Finance approval thresholds and permitted publication windows.
Whether national rules require consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which calculations can the existing {ERP} perform without custom code?
How accurately do proposed assumptions explain historical actual material costs?
new_work: Review extracted quotation changes and ambiguous terms.
Maintain conversion tables and landed cost rules.
Resolve failed imports and reconcile published versions.
Compare forecasts with actuals and revise assumptions.

tasks.short: Find and qualify environmentally preferable raw materials for manufacturing.

steps.what: Define material performance requirements and acceptable environmental evidence.
Search approved suppliers and material catalogues in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Request specifications, certificates, quotations and samples through the {EMAIL}.
Review supplier specifications, certificates and environmental claims.

loop.input: Supplier specifications, certificates and claims against the approved material specification.
loop.output: Evidence matrix with source passages, validity dates, limitations and missing evidence.
loop.check: Check identifiers, dates and required fields; quality staff verify relevance and authenticity separately.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; missing or conflicting evidence blocks qualification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence arrives in varied documents, and important limitations appear in prose.

steps.what: Run material trials and inspect manufacturing performance.
Compare landed costs, evidence coverage and measured material performance.
Select the material and agree qualification limits with quality and production.
Record approved materials, restrictions and evidence expiry dates in the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: The {PROCUREMENT} filters candidate materials and the {WORKFLOW} sends standard evidence requests to authorised supplier contacts through the {EMAIL}. A bounded loop builds a source-linked evidence matrix from the {DOCS}, while deterministic comparisons show cost, trial results and missing evidence. Quality staff approve qualification before the {PROCUREMENT} records permitted uses and expiry dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Environmental claims were difficult to compare, evidence was scattered, and qualification restrictions were separated from purchasing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records and request workflows handle the routine work. Bounded extraction makes varied supplier documents easier to review without treating claims as verified facts.
tasks.still_hard: Biodegradability and toxicity depend on conditions and intended use. Trials, certificate verification, performance tradeoffs and supplier evidence gaps remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a material is safe and suitable in the actual manufacturing process, including environmental tradeoffs across its lifecycle.

ambition.what: Qualified substitute material register with permitted applications for production planners.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on promising substitutions and fewer hours comparing dossiers. They can recommend substitutions within documented qualification limits; quality retains release authority.

reach.task: Define material qualification and requalification criteria.
reach.learn: Evidence validity, sampling, trial acceptance and change control.

reach.task: Plan production using qualified substitute materials.
reach.learn: Application restrictions, yield differences and substitution dependencies.

evidence.claim: Structured qualification records and expiry reminders can be configured without model judgement.
Document extraction can organise supplier evidence but cannot establish material safety or environmental suitability.

assumptions: The company manufactures products and already has a material qualification process.
Time shares describe active task effort across contributing roles.
Catalogue filtering uses existing structured fields; missing attributes create evidence gaps.
Automatic requests use approved templates and contacts and make no purchasing commitment.
Build estimates cover the information workflow; physical trial duration and laboratory costs are additional.
GDPR applies to supplier contacts. EU AI Act applicability and consultation duties under national rules are checked during setup.
unknowns: Material categories, intended uses and applicable product requirements.
Availability and reliability of catalogue attributes.
Who verifies certificates and approves trials.
Trial capacity, lead times and external testing needs.
Permissions for supplier communications and qualification updates.
Any employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which test methods and certifications substantiate each environmental claim for the intended use?
Which existing qualification fields can represent restrictions and evidence expiry?
new_work: Review extracted claims and verify supporting evidence.
Follow up missing documents and expired certificates.
Maintain request templates and qualification criteria.
Requalify materials when supplier processes or product applications change.

tasks.short: Assess supplier manufacturing capability through visits, observations and measured evidence.

steps.what: Arrange the supplier visit, attendees and evidence request through the {EMAIL}.
Prepare the assessment brief from supplier records and submitted documents.

loop.input: Supplier dossier, previous findings and approved assessment checklist.
loop.output: Brief with evidence references, outstanding questions and proposed verification points.
loop.check: Require a source for factual statements; assessor checks coverage and visit priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported statements become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier narratives and previous findings contain context that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Observe production, question staff and witness capability measurements at the supplier site.
Compile measured capacity, quality results and checklist completion in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Challenge findings and judge sustainable capacity, process control and delivery risk.
Write the capability assessment and proposed qualification conditions.

loop.input: Recorded observations, measurements, assessor judgement and required corrective actions.
loop.output: Draft assessment separating observed evidence, supplier claims and assessor conclusions.
loop.check: Reconcile figures to measurements; assessor verifies every finding and qualification condition.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved evidence stays explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful report must explain contextual observations and the assessor's reasoning.

steps.what: Approve the assessment and qualification status in the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} prepares visit logistics and a structured assessment record, while bounded loops draft the brief and report from evidence in the {DOCS}. Configured forms calculate measurement summaries and flag missing evidence; the assessor conducts the visit and makes the capability judgement. The quality manager approves qualification status in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The essential evidence comes from physical observation and questioning. Preparation and reporting also relied on disconnected documents and repeated transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured assessment forms and source-linked drafting can reduce paperwork around the visit. They do not replace direct observation or establish that supplier claims are true.
tasks.still_hard: A visit may show a staged or unrepresentative process. Assessors must judge sustained capacity, challenge explanations and follow up corrective actions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice inconsistencies on site, ask revealing follow-up questions and judge whether observed performance can be sustained.
tasks.altitude: Visits and capability decisions remain central to the week. Less preparation and report writing creates more time to verify corrective actions; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Verify closure of supplier corrective actions.
reach.learn: Root-cause evidence, representative sampling and effectiveness checks.

reach.task: Use qualified supplier capacity in production plans.
reach.learn: Demonstrated capacity, utilisation limits and qualification conditions.

evidence.claim: Assessment forms, completeness checks and measurement summaries can use existing configuration.
Drafting support can reduce assessment paperwork while physical observation and capability judgement stay human.

assumptions: The assessment includes a physical supplier visit and an existing qualification checklist.
Time shares describe active assessment effort and exclude travel and waiting.
Measurement summaries use structured fields; narrative findings remain available to the assessor.
Visit communications require approval because access arrangements and confidentiality terms vary.
No worker recording or individual performance scoring is introduced. GDPR applies to personal data in notes; national rules and site permissions govern collection.
The EU AI Act assessment covers the actual drafting use and any later expansion.
unknowns: Current assessment templates and supplier qualification authority.
Supplier permission for notes, photographs and document storage.
Whether assessment forms must work offline.
Available {PROCUREMENT} qualification fields and access rights.
Any employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which capability measures best predict sustained performance for the relevant manufacturing process?
Can the existing assessment configuration retain evidence links and qualification conditions?
new_work: Review draft briefs and reports against original evidence.
Maintain checklists, calculation rules and report templates.
Resolve incomplete measurements and synchronisation failures.
Check that qualification conditions and corrective actions remain current.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager spends less time assembling evidence and maintaining comparisons, and more time testing operational choices, qualifying alternatives and challenging supplier capability. Any added authority should be explicit and bounded by budget, quality and service limits.
reach: Logistics analyst: build and interpret operational scenarios.
Production planning clerk: connect qualified materials, supplier capacity and production schedules.
Quality control systems manager: strengthen qualification evidence and corrective-action verification.
Project management specialist: coordinate implementation dependencies and acceptance.
skills_to_grow: Environmental evidence boundaries and material qualification.
Data reconciliation, units and source traceability.
Supplier interviewing and physical capability assessment.
role.ambitious_version: Run a quarterly supply chain options review combining environmental scenarios, material cost exposure and qualified alternatives, with funded trials and explicit decisions recorded for operations and finance.
